title: Review Finding v1
description: A single code-review finding emitted by an automated reviewer (lamella-skills code-review or canopy plan-review phase). Captures issues, security concerns, or style violations discovered during structured code review.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Always '1.0' for this schema.

finding_id.description: Unique identifier for this finding, assigned by the producer as a ULID. Enables correlation and deduplication across review runs.

severity.description: Severity level of this finding. Closed enum for exhaustive consumer matching. Matches threat-severity-v1 vocabulary.

category.description: Classification category of the finding. Examples: 'correctness', 'security', 'style', 'performance', 'maintainability'. Producers may define project-specific categories; consumers should tolerate unknown values gracefully.

title.description: Short human-readable title of the finding. Suitable for display in lists or summaries.

description.description: Detailed explanation of the issue, including context, rationale, and impact. May contain markdown formatting.

confidence.description: Confidence level that this finding is valid. 'confirmed' = verified or obvious; 'likely' = high probability; 'speculative' = hypothesis requiring human review.

tier.description: Classification of whether this finding blocks the review gate. 'merge' = blocking issue that must be resolved; 'detail' = informational, does not block approval.

file_path.description: Path to the file containing the issue, relative to repository root. Null for findings that span multiple files or have no specific file location.

line_start.description: Starting line number of the code section containing the issue. Null if not applicable or file_path is null.

line_end.description: Ending line number of the code section containing the issue. Null if not applicable or file_path is null.

autofix_class.description: Classifies whether and how easily an autofix could resolve this finding. 'none' = no automated fix available; 'trivial' = simple substitution/format fix; 'moderate' = requires minor logic changes; 'invasive' = requires significant refactoring.

suggested_fix.description: If available, a suggested code change or explanation of how to resolve the issue. May include code snippets or prose guidance. Null if no fix is suggested.

related_finding_ids.description: List of other finding IDs that are related to this finding (e.g., similar issues in the same codebase, or a root cause with multiple symptoms). Empty array if none.
